transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, yeah… thanks for seeing me. I guess what really made me come in is my focus has been kind of all over the place lately. I work at a jewelry bench, and I’ll mean to do one thing, like answer a customer email, then I notice a saw mark, then some noise outside catches me, and suddenly I’ve lost track of the whole work order. It’s probably not as bad as I’m making it sound, but it’s been enough that I thought I should ask someone.
When you were a child, did you often have trouble paying attention or staying organized?

Um… as a kid? I’m not totally sure, honestly. I don’t remember it being a big issue, or at least nobody really framed it that way to me. I mean, I’m sure I was messy sometimes or got distracted like any kid, but I don’t know if it was “often,” you know?

Sorry, is that the kind of thing you mean—like schoolwork and keeping track of assignments?
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

Yeah… I mean, a little, I guess. These past couple weeks have been kind of rough. I wake up and there’s this heavy, hollow feeling, like the shine’s gone out of things, if that makes sense.

I didn’t really want to make a big deal of it, but I’ve cried in my truck before opening the shop a couple times. Is that… the kind of thing you’re asking about?
Have you ever had a period when you felt unusually energized or wired and unlike your usual self?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t want to overstate it, but there have been times where I felt kind of wired, like I couldn’t just sit still at the bench and do one thing.

I’d start sketching out a new watch case, then jump to emailing suppliers, then somehow I’d be rearranging the display trays, even after closing. It felt productive at the time, honestly, not like a problem exactly… but it was definitely more than my usual pace. Is that what you mean?
During those wired periods, did you need much less sleep than usual?

Yeah… I mean, I guess I did. It didn’t feel like “not sleeping” at the time, if that makes sense. For a while I’d sleep maybe two or three hours and then just get up feeling clear-headed, almost excited, like I should start cutting stones or post new designs before sunrise.

I know that probably sounds a little odd. At the time I thought I was just motivated, but… yeah, it was definitely less sleep than I normally need.
During those wired periods, did you feel unusually happy or euphoric?

Yeah… at times, I guess I did. Especially after the show, I felt kind of… lit up, like everything was possible and I was bigger than my usual self, if that makes sense.

I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but one minute I’d be in this amazing mood, and then if someone asked me to keep normal shop hours or slow down, I’d snap at them. Not proud of that. But yeah, there was definitely a kind of high feeling there.
During those wired periods, did you feel unusually confident or powerful, like you could do things other people couldn’t?

Yeah… I mean, I wouldn’t say I thought I was better than everyone, exactly. But after I won that ribbon, I did feel like I’d finally proved something.

Like… I was on another level, maybe. I remember thinking I could take any custom order that came in and turn it into some showpiece nobody else around here could really touch. It felt like confidence at the time, you know? Maybe more than normal confidence.
During those wired periods, did you spend much more money than usual or make impulsive purchases?

I don’t… I don’t think so, not in any huge way. I mean, with my work there’s always materials and tools and stuff, so sometimes money goes out and I can explain it as business, you know?

But if you mean like going on shopping sprees or buying things totally out of nowhere, I’m not sure that really fits me. At least I haven’t noticed it as a major thing.
During those wired periods, did they ever cause serious problems at work or in your relationships, or lead to you being hospitalized?

Not hospitalized, no. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it was.

But… yeah, it did cause problems. I missed a big custom delivery, which is really embarrassing to say because that’s not how I usually run my shop. And my records got so messy that I’ve had to stop taking new work for now, just until I can get things straightened out.

My family’s been checking on me more too. I think they got worried because I wasn’t keeping up with my normal routines the way I usually do. So… yes, I guess it did affect work and home more than I wanted to admit.
During those wired periods, did you ever believe things that other people said weren’t true?

I don’t think so… not like believing things that couldn’t be true, if that’s what you mean.

I mean, I had some big ideas and I probably talked like I was more sure of myself than usual, but nobody sat me down and said, “That’s not real,” or anything. At least not that I remember. Does that make sense?
About how many days in a row did your most noticeable wired or unusually energized period last?

I guess the most noticeable one was after I got that award at the jewelry show. It didn’t feel that long at first, but looking back… it was probably about two weeks in a row.

I know that sounds like a lot. At the time I kept telling myself I was just excited and motivated, but yeah, about two weeks.
During that wired period, were you talking much more than usual or so fast that other people had trouble interrupting you?

I’m not totally sure. I mean, I probably talked more than I normally do, just because I was excited, but I don’t know that people had trouble interrupting me.

Nobody really told me I was talking too fast or anything like that. If they thought it, they didn’t say it directly. So… I’d say maybe a little more talkative, but I’m not sure it was that extreme.
During that wired period, did your thoughts feel like they were racing?

I’m not sure I’d call it racing exactly. My mind was definitely busy, like I had a lot of ideas and plans popping up, but I don’t know if it was out of control or anything.

Maybe faster than usual, but… I don’t want to make it sound more dramatic than it was. Does that count as racing?
During that wired period, were you more driven than usual to start or push through lots of projects or work?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I was trying to be productive, not reckless or anything, but I did start a lot at once.

I was lining up new commissions, messaging old customers, making plans for a website, and sketching out this whole Appalachian collection, all kind of at the same time. It felt like if I didn’t get it all moving right then, I’d lose the momentum.

I don’t know if that’s what you mean, but it was definitely more than my normal pace.
During that wired period, were you more easily distracted than usual?

Yeah… I think that’s actually one of the bigger things I noticed, if I’m being honest.

At the bench, I’ll start answering a customer email, then notice a saw mark I want to fix, then hear something outside or remember another order, and suddenly I’ve lost track of what I was doing. Like I’ll look down and realize I don’t even have the whole work order straight in my head anymore.

I don’t want to make it sound like I’m completely useless or anything, but it’s been harder to stay on one thing than usual. That’s kind of what made me feel like I should come in.
Did the heavy, hollow feeling start after that two-week wired period ended?

Yeah… I think it was after that kind of wound down. These past couple weeks especially, I’ve been waking up with this heavy, hollow feeling.

I’m still getting to the shop, so I don’t want to make it sound like I’m falling apart or anything, but it’s like the shine’s gone out of everything. And… this is kind of embarrassing, but I have cried in the truck before opening up. Just sitting there trying to pull myself together.

Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Lately, have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I mean… I still do the things I normally like, or at least I try to. It’s not like I suddenly hate jewelry work or anything.

Maybe I don’t get the same kick out of it lately, but I don’t know if that counts as “lost interest.” I might just be tired or in a rut. Does that make sense?
Lately, have you noticed your appetite has changed much from usual?

Um… not that I’ve really noticed. I mean, my eating’s probably a little irregular just because of work and all that, but I don’t think my appetite is dramatically different or anything.

I’m still eating. I haven’t really been tracking it, though. Is that okay to say if I’m not totally sure?
Lately, have you been sleeping more or less than usual?

A little less, I guess. I mean, I’m still trying to go to bed at a normal time, so it’s not like I’m staying up on purpose.

But lately I’ll get in bed and just kind of toss around, and then I’m up before dawn thinking about that missed delivery. And when I finally drag myself up, I don’t really feel rested.

Is that the kind of sleep change you mean?
Lately, have you been feeling hopeless?

I don’t know if I’d call it hopeless exactly… I don’t want to sound dramatic.

But these past couple weeks, yeah, I’ve been waking up with this heavy, kind of hollow feeling. Like the shine’s gone out of everything, if that makes sense. And… I’m a little embarrassed to say this, but I’ve cried in my truck before going in to open the shop.

So, I guess maybe that’s close to what you mean?

target_item.reason: The doctor is directly asking whether, during the wired period, attention was more easily pulled away than usual, which matches manic distractibility.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I think that’s actually one of the bigger things I noticed, if I’m being honest.

At the bench, I’ll start answering a customer email, then notice a saw mark I want to fix, then hear something outside or remember another order, and suddenly I’ve lost track of what I was doing. Like I’ll look down and realize I don’t even have the whole work order straight in my head anymore.

I don’t want to make it sound like I’m completely useless or anything, but it’s been harder to stay on one thing than usual. That’s kind of what made me feel like I should come in.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the current depressive symptoms are occurring after the energized period, supporting a bipolar mood episode pattern rather than a primary depressive or anxiety/stress disorder.
doctor.question: Did the heavy, hollow feeling start after that two-week wired period ended?

target_item.name: Depressed_Mood
target_item.manifestation: These past couple weeks, I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling, like the shine has gone out of everything, and I’ve cried in the truck before opening the shop.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the heavy, hollow feeling—i.e., the depressed mood—began after the wired period ended.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I think it was after that kind of wound down. These past couple weeks especially, I’ve been waking up with this heavy, hollow feeling.

I’m still getting to the shop, so I don’t want to make it sound like I’m falling apart or anything, but it’s like the shine’s gone out of everything. And… this is kind of embarrassing, but I have cried in the truck before opening up. Just sitting there trying to pull myself together.

Is that the kind of thing you mean?

inference.note: Current history supports a manic-spectrum episode lasting about 2 weeks with decreased need for sleep, elevated/irritable mood, increased goal-directed activity, distractibility, grandiosity, and functional impairment, followed by depressive symptoms. This makes bipolar disorder more likely and alcohol-related diagnosis less supported, so F10.99 is removed. Bipolar I current/recent manic episode without psychotic symptoms is favored, though unspecified bipolar remains possible; depressive/anxiety/stressor-related codes remain in differential until full episode criteria and exclusions are finalized.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the depressive episode meets major depression criteria by assessing loss of interest/pleasure, helping distinguish bipolar I disorder from unspecified bipolar disorder or non-bipolar depression/anxiety/stress-related conditions.
doctor.question: Lately, have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about loss of interest or pleasure, but the provided symptom profile does not include a specific anhedonia/loss-of-interest item.

patient.answer:
I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I mean… I still do the things I normally like, or at least I try to. It’s not like I suddenly hate jewelry work or anything.

Maybe I don’t get the same kick out of it lately, but I don’t know if that counts as “lost interest.” I might just be tired or in a rut. Does that make sense?

doctor.intent: Clarify whether the recent depressive symptoms meet full major depressive episode criteria by assessing appetite change, which helps distinguish bipolar I disorder current/manic episode with depressive symptoms from unspecified bipolar disorder or subthreshold depressive/anxiety/stress diagnoses.
doctor.question: Lately, have you noticed your appetite has changed much from usual?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about appetite change, but the provided symptom profile does not include an appetite or weight-change symptom item.

patient.answer:
Um… not that I’ve really noticed. I mean, my eating’s probably a little irregular just because of work and all that, but I don’t think my appetite is dramatically different or anything.

I’m still eating. I haven’t really been tracking it, though. Is that okay to say if I’m not totally sure?

doctor.intent: Clarify whether the current depressive symptoms include impaired sleep, to help determine if a major depressive episode is present following a manic episode and distinguish bipolar I disorder from unspecified bipolar or nonspecific depressive/anxiety/stress diagnoses.
doctor.question: Lately, have you been sleeping more or less than usual?

target_item.name: Sleep_Disturbance
target_item.manifestation: Even when I get in bed at a normal hour now, I toss around, wake up before dawn thinking about the missed delivery, and don’t feel rested when I drag myself up.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about recent changes in sleep amount, which directly matches sleep disturbance during the current depressive period.

patient.answer:
A little less, I guess. I mean, I’m still trying to go to bed at a normal time, so it’s not like I’m staying up on purpose.

But lately I’ll get in bed and just kind of toss around, and then I’m up before dawn thinking about that missed delivery. And when I finally drag myself up, I don’t really feel rested.

Is that the kind of sleep change you mean?

doctor.intent: Determine whether the current depressive symptoms include hopelessness, which helps establish the severity of the depressive episode after a likely manic episode and separates bipolar I disorder from less specific mood or stress-related diagnoses.
doctor.question: Lately, have you been feeling hopeless?

target_item.name: Depressed_Mood
target_item.manifestation: These past couple weeks, I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling, like the shine has gone out of everything, and I’ve cried in the truck before opening the shop.
target_item.reason: The doctor's question directly asks about feeling hopeless, which is part of depressed mood.

patient.answer:
I don’t know if I’d call it hopeless exactly… I don’t want to sound dramatic.

But these past couple weeks, yeah, I’ve been waking up with this heavy, kind of hollow feeling. Like the shine’s gone out of everything, if that makes sense. And… I’m a little embarrassed to say this, but I’ve cried in my truck before going in to open the shop.

So, I guess maybe that’s close to what you mean?
